steps.title: Declare the parameters
notes: Upskin is off by default. Its group has only two values of its own, min_width and overlap, plus a complete hatch sub-group with a smaller hatch distance of 0.08 mm.
Single layer in the comment is the key point: only the next layer above is compared, so each top surface gets exactly one layer of upskin.

lines: // Off by default. Only the next layer above is compared: an area that
// is not covered there is upskin (top surface). min_width and overlap

steps.title: Read the values from the profile
notes: part.upskin holds the switch, both distances and a complete HATCH object read by read_hatch: pattern, hatch distance, rotation and the rest, exactly as for the volume hatch.

steps.title: Find the upskin area
notes: splitSkin is a builtin of the island: it returns the part of the current layer that the layer above does not cover. On the step block that is the whole step at z = 1.98 mm, because the next layer (2.01 mm) is above the step top.
Downskin wins where both apply: process_part_island subtracts the downskin from the upskin.

lines: // splitSkin uses the current layer of makeExposureLayer implicitly.
let l_us = l_part.upskin.enabled ? SKIN.split_upskin_one_layer(a_island, l_part.upskin) : ISL.empty();

steps.title: Drop thin slivers
notes: ISL.opening removes everything narrower than min_width. Why that matters: on a sloped top, each layer sticks out by only t / tan(angle) beyond the next one, 52 µm at 30°. Without the opening every layer would get a narrow upskin strip of very short vectors.
With the default 0.1 mm, slopes steeper than about 17° get no upskin strips at all.

lines: * splitSkin compares only with the next layer above (single-layer
* Like the downskin, thin slivers (narrower than min_width, mm) are
* removed; along sloped top walls the single-layer comparison would
* otherwise produce a thin upskin strip in every layer.

steps.title: Grow into the volume, then hatch
notes: process_part_hatches grows the upskin by overlap, clips it to the hatch area and removes it from the volume. The two hatches overlap at their joint instead of leaving a gap.
On the left this gives 7.99 × 9.78 mm of upskin at 0.08 mm: about 977 mm of yellow vectors, and ATU reports 976.78 mm for that layer. The volume hatch drops from 2326 mm to 1544 mm.

lines: // The skin areas are grown by their 'overlap' (mm) before they are
// clipped to the hatch area. The skin hatch then reaches a little into
// the neighboring volume, which bonds both areas and avoids a gap at
hatch_area(a_ctx, a_result, l_us_area, l_part.upskin.hatch, BSID.hatch_upskin, l_id, l_b, false);

steps.title: Laser settings and order
notes: The upskin hatch (BSID 520) runs at 220 W and 900 mm/s, slower than the volume hatch (280 W, 1200 mm/s): with the smaller hatch distance that melts the top surface more thoroughly. Scan order 50 puts it after the volume and core hatches.
On the top layer of the block (z = 6 mm) the whole area is upskin and the volume hatch disappears.

recipes.title: Upskin on by default
recipes.why: Most of your parts have visible top surfaces.
recipes.result: New profiles start with the upskin switched on. Untick Upskin in Try it to compare.

recipes.title: Upskin also on shallow slopes
recipes.why: A slightly sloped top surface should get its upskin strips as well.
recipes.result: Strips from 50 µm are kept: slopes up to about 31° get an upskin strip on every layer. Try it in the Sloped top view.

recipes.title: More overlap with the volume
recipes.why: A visible seam between the upskin and the volume hatch.
recipes.result: The yellow hatch reaches 0.2 mm into the volume. Drag Overlap in the Top view.

recipes.title: Slower upskin
recipes.why: Even more energy for a smoother top surface.
recipes.result: Upskin default 800 mm/s. For one profile, change Scanning › Upskin hatch › speed in the dialog instead.
